items.title: Trump said colleges would ‘go to hell very quickly’ without foreign students. New enrollment just fell 18%, costing them billions in tuition
items.summary:
New international students at U.S. colleges fell 18% in the 2025–26 school year, to 228,123, the Institute of International Education said Monday in its annual Open Doors report . The first look at this fall points to a second straight drop. In IIE’s fall 2026 snapshot of more than 800 schools, new international enrollment fell another 15%.

The total looks calmer: 1,146,163 international students, down 3%. But that count includes 335,785 graduates on Optional Practical Training, the program that lets them work in the U.S. after their degree. That group rose 14%, and it pays no tuition. Take it out and the number of international students enrolled in classes fell about 8%, by Fortune’s math. That’s about 73,000 fewer students paying tuition.

The president saw this coming. At a cabinet meeting in August 2025 , defending a plan to admit 600,000 Chinese students, Trump said that without them, “our college system would go to hell very quickly and it wouldn’t be the top colleges. It would be colleges that struggle on the bottom.” His base pushed back. Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene said that if keeping Chinese students out made some schools fail, “these schools should fail anyways because they are being propped up by the CCP.”

Since then, his administration has moved the other way. In May 2025 the State Department paused student visa interviews, then restarted them with expanded social media vetting. A travel ban that started with 19 countries grew to 39, plus the Palestinian territory, on Jan. 1. In July, DHS finalized a rule replacing open-ended student status with a fixed…
items.t: Trump said colleges would ‘go to hell very quickly’ without foreign students. New enrollment just fell 18%, costing them billions in tuition

items.title: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. serves Trump Jollibee in a moment of culinary diplomacy

“Jollibee is a very, very popular chain, and one of their main products is fried chicken,” Marcos said at the opening of his bilateral meeting with Trump on Wednesday. “We are very proud to say that we have surpassed KFC in the United States in terms of popularity.”

While in Manila, Trump announced that he’d agreed “a very big trade deal, the biggest trade deal we’ve ever made so far” with the Philippines, yet offered no details. Marcos’s office has not confirmed the agreement of a trade deal.

The delivery was culinary diplomacy for a chain that’s become a national symbol at home and has ambitions to break into the U.S. market.

Started in 1975 as an ice cream parlor by Filipino businessman Tony Tan Caktiong, Jollibee is best known for its “Chickenjoy” fried chicken and a sweet-style spaghetti topped with sliced hot dogs. The chain has more than 1,600 stores across 17 countries, according to its website. 

Its parent, Jollibee Foods Corporation, runs a portfolio of about 20 brands—including Chinese-food chain Chowking, dim sum chain Tim Ho Wan, and U.S. burger chain Smashburger—with more than 10,000 stores and cafés across 33 countries. With $5.3 billion in annual revenue, Jollibee ranks No. 71 on the Fortune Southeast Asia 500.

In January, Jollibee said it would…

items.title: Nvidia’s earnings boom meets a governance test
items.summary:
Good morning. Nvidia’s third-quarter earnings call, the first for CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, came less than a week after Jensen Huang resigned. The company delivered stronger-than-expected results, but the leadership transition and a new emphasis on board oversight put governance and regulatory compliance front and center.

“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing,” Kress said Tuesday on the call. 

Board Chair Harvey Jones ended speculation about Huang’s return. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said. The board is conducting an independent investigation after Huang disclosed personal behavior inconsistent with company standards. 

Heidrick & Struggles has been retained to conduct an internal and external search for Huang’s permanent replacement. 

Jones said the board is “enhancing our oversight capacity going forward.” He noted the formation of the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to oversee national security policies, export-control compliance and global trade risks. Nvidia’s national security and trade compliance teams will report directly to the committee and to Kress for day-to-day operations.

The move underscores the growing importance of compliance for Nvidia and its new leadership amid questions about the potential diversion of advanced AI chips to China.

The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security announced Monday an interim final rule addressing remote access to advanced computing technology through overseas…
items.t: Nvidia’s earnings boom meets a governance test

items.title: I’ve coached the world’s most marketable athlete for 8 years. New CEOs should copy how her team handles expert advice
items.summary:
There are a lot of new CEOs coming into the market right now. Challenger, Gray & Christmas counted 1,337 CEO exits in the first nine months of this year, including 111 in September. On September 1, John Ternus took over at Apple , with Tim Cook staying on as executive chairman.

When someone takes over a new leadership role, they’re getting a ton of advice. Even the good advice is often too much. “This is what worked really well for us.” “This has been a problem this whole time.” It comes from staff members and even the former CEO.

It’s from the experience and knowledge of all these other people, which is fantastic. But the problem I see is it’s an overdose. You start to lose touch with your own instincts, your own gut. And when you must make the tough decisions your gut already knows, you hesitate.

Keeping the circle tight 

For the past eight years, I have coached Aryna Sabalenka, a multiple Grand Slam champion who has spent more than 100 weeks at world No. 1. She was just named the most marketable athlete in the world, out of all sports. You can imagine how many people are approaching us these days.

Anton Dubrov is her tennis coach. I am her performance coach. A big part of our job is filtering. Whether we’re speaking with specialists, agents or Aryna directly, we’re constantly filtering what’s getting through and who has the access.

In 2022, her serve was falling apart. She finished that year with 428 double faults, more than anyone else on the tour. In San Jose, she lost the same way, frustrated and crying, talking about how we’d done everything. I remember…
items.t: I’ve coached the world’s most marketable athlete for 8 years. New CEOs should copy how her team handles expert advice

items.title: ‘The Romans are laughing at us’: physical AI founder raises $97 million in quest to stop wasting time with archaic infrastructure maintenance
items.summary:
Alex Hawkinson keeps a collection of Roman artifacts at BrightAI’s robot demo center, and he has a saying to go with them: “The Romans are laughing at us.”

Think of the way the Romans inspected their roads, Hawkinson told Fortune : “They sent teams of technicians out periodically on schedule” to check on their infrastructure. Two thousand years later, power companies, water utilities, and pipeline operators still do. In his telling, two out of three of those trips turn up nothing to fix, and the failures that matter happen in between visits anyway.

Hawkinson is convinced this can change, and investors are paying for the idea. BrightAI said Wednesday it has raised $97 million in a round led by Smith Point Capital , the growth-stage firm started by former Salesforce co-CEO Keith Block. GE Vernova, already a BrightAI customer, also invested, along with Cobalt Capital, Marlinspike Partners, Zero Infinity Partners as well as existing backers Khosla Ventures, Inspired Capital, and Upfront Ventures. The round brings total funding to $184 million and values BrightAI at $750 million, according to a person familiar with the matter. Hawkinson insisted he “doesn’t care” about so-called unicorn status: The point is bring infrastructure out of the ancient Roman era.

His pitch has three parts. Replace scheduled human inspections with sensors and AI that watch infrastructure all the time. Go after what BrightAI estimates is more than $7 trillion a year in waste worldwide. And along the way, create a kind of data that has never existed: a continuous record of how pipes, poles, and pumps…
items.t: ‘The Romans are laughing at us’: physical AI founder raises $97 million in quest to stop wasting time with archaic infrastructure maintenance

items.title: We built the AI study tool every parent wants. Almost nobody used it
items.summary:
I run Tutorela , a U.S. tutoring marketplace that sells human tutoring, with AI for students between sessions. I’m saying that up front because this piece argues for that model, and because we learned the lesson behind it the hard way.

Alpha School has become the national test case for AI-first education, and it’s now expanding into public schools in Texas and South Carolina. As districts decide how much of the school day to hand to software, they should hear what happened when we gave students the best learning tool we could build.

We built it. They didn’t come. 

For 15 years we’ve run Limud Naim, a tutoring marketplace in Israel whose tutors have taught more than 500,000 private lessons. To fill the gap between those lessons, we built a math learning and practice app with more than 10,000 exercises. Every problem came with a full solution in text and video, and we made the whole thing a game, with progress and rewards, so practice would feel less like homework. A year ago we added an AI assistant that could walk a student through any step, any time, for free.

By any product standard it was the best a student could get. Only about 10% of students used it, and most of those who started didn’t stick around. The exercises were excellent and the AI was patient and clear, but none of that mattered, because the students weren’t showing up.

We’re not the only ones. 

A two-year randomized trial in 18 Tennessee middle schools, published this year by the National Bureau of Economic Research , found the same thing with Khanmigo , Khan Academy’s AI tutor. Nearly every student…
items.t: We built the AI study tool every parent wants. Almost nobody used it

The same kid who fell in love with Rockstar’s games back then now gets to spend every day helping to create those worlds as an animation programmer at the studio in Edinburgh. Nvidia has also forged a strong commercial alliance with Saudi Arabia, with Huang among a select group of U.S. tech leaders invited to meet with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman during his much-feted visit to the White House last November. 

During the visit, Elon Musk announced a 500-MW data center in partnership with Saudi government-backed AI company, Humain , which will be powered by Nvidia’s computing chips. 

Trump also hosted Mohammed bin Salman, alongside Huang and Elon Musk, at the U.S.-Saudi Investment Forum on November 19 last year. 

Just hours later, the U.S. Commerce Department authorized the export of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell GB300 chips to both G42 and Humain. Earlier in the day, Humain said it planned…
items.t: Does the Nvidia turmoil spell trouble for the Gulf’s AI ambitions?

items.title: Bristol Myers Squibb CEO says America’s edge in new drugs is ‘not a birthright’ as the U.S. loses its measles elimination status
items.summary:
On the day the U.S. officially lost its measles-elimination status, Bristol Myers Squibb CEO Chris Boerner had a warning for the country that went beyond one virus.

“It’s a reminder,” Boerner said Tuesday at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit, after Fortune ’s Diane Brady opened their conversation with the news. The U.S. leads the world in new medicines, he said: 90% of them launch here, often two to three years before other rich countries get them. “That’s a real benefit that we have, but it’s not a birthright.”

On Tuesday, the Pan American Health Organization said the U.S. no longer meets the standard it first cleared in 2000: no single chain of measles transmission lasting 12 months or longer. The CDC has counted more than 5,400 cases so far in 2026, after 2,289 last year, many of them in outbreaks that began in close-knit Mennonite communities and spread, CBS News reported . Mexico and Bolivia lost their status too. Canada lost its status last year.

The numbers behind the decision have been building. In the 2025–26 school year, 92.4% of U.S. kindergartners had their MMR shots, CDC data show . That was down from 95.2% before the pandemic and under the 95% that epidemiologists say measles herd immunity requires. Exemptions hit a record 4.2%.

Boerner didn’t name Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. or any specific policy. He did spell out what he thinks keeps the U.S. ahead: a public-private partnership built around the NIH, a deep biotech scene, access to capital, drugmakers that work from discovery to sale, and “an FDA that’s the sort of global standard.”…
items.t: Bristol Myers Squibb CEO says America’s edge in new drugs is ‘not a birthright’ as the U.S. loses its measles elimination status

items.title: The Guardian view on the Milburn report: a manifesto for youth participation | Editorial
items.summary:
This is not a rerun of failed welfare cuts, but young people who rely on benefits cannot be expected to take promised opportunities on trust

The gap between the state’s investment in young people compared with older generations has more than doubled in two decades. At the same time, the number of 16- to 24-year-olds who are neither in education, employment or training (Neet) has climbed to 1 million. In Europe, only Romania has a higher Neet rate.

Alan Milburn’s message is that this amounts to a “moral crisis” which the British state must urgently address. Asked to write a review about young people and work, he has produced a “manifesto” for placing the broken social contract between generations at the heart of government. On Tuesday, his proposals for far-reaching changes to welfare, health, education and employment were on their way to becoming government policy as he was chosen to lead a new Youth Opportunities Unit.

items.title: The Guardian view on climate and debt: a vicious cycle the world must break at Cop31 | Editorial
items.summary:
Poor countries are paying creditors instead of preparing for climate disasters. The international financial system must stop deepening their vulnerability

The catastrophe that struck Nepal’s Himalayas in August began with a collapsing glacier. An avalanche of ice and rock unleashed deadly floods, sweeping away villages, bridges and roads, and leaving thousands dead or missing. It illustrated the dangers posed by global heating to the Himalayas’ increasingly unstable glaciers. Nepal lost a tenth of its electricity generation. Reconstruction will cost about $5bn. Yet the Loss and Damage Fund, hailed as a historic breakthrough at the 2022 UN climate summit, has earmarked just $20m for Nepal – less than 5% of the $482m that Kathmandu must pay its external public creditors this year.

items.title: Will the Milburn review come good or go south? Either way, we’ll always have Eurovision
items.summary:
The announcement of state plans to engage with young people told us nothing we hadn’t already heard, but it still felt momentous

It’s one of the country’s worst kept secrets. There can’t be anyone left who hasn’t heard of Alan Milburn’s Neets review, let alone read most of it too. It feels as if it’s become part of the fabric of our society for the past six months. There will be a Neets-shaped hole in our lives when it’s over.

Not a day has gone by without some part of it being leaked to the media. Seldom has a pitch been so icomprehensively rolled. Milburn has been out and about giving interviews to everyone – regardless of whether they wanted one or not. I rather suspect the reason Royal Mail lied about calling to collect my parcel return yesterday was because the driver found himself cornered by Milburn for a couple of hours and was unable to complete his round. Either that, or Royal Mail has a fleet of vans crisscrossing the country whose sole purpose is to make sure they never deliver anything. Ghost vans.
